# how-to-web Product Card

> Machine-readable reconstruction guidance for the how-to-web Product Card block.

This path documents a framework-independent Product Card. Coding agents should use the Build DNA as the primary reconstruction contract. The examples demonstrate three documented variants and must not replace the generic contract.

## Primary

- [Build DNA](./build-dna.json): Canonical machine-readable reconstruction contract. Read this first.
- [Product Card reference](./index.md): Concise LLM-friendly explanation of anatomy, behavior, responsive rules, accessibility and constraints.
- [Human reference](./): Interactive showcase and review guidance.

## Variants

- [Premium Retail data](./examples/premium-retail.json): Image-led retail variant with multiple product views.
- [Premium Retail example](./examples/premium-retail.html): Rendered Premium Retail reference.
- [Technical Retail data](./examples/technical-retail.json): Specification-heavy comparison variant.
- [Technical Retail example](./examples/technical-retail.html): Rendered Technical Retail reference.
- [Compact data](./examples/compact.json): Dense listing variant with reduced secondary information.
- [Compact example](./examples/compact.html): Rendered Compact reference.

## Agent request patterns

Supported entry points include:

- generic Product Card reconstruction,
- Premium Retail,
- Technical Retail,
- Compact,
- adaptation into an existing project.

All entry points resolve to the same Build DNA. A named variant narrows the desired presentation but does not override Purpose, Constraints, Behavior, Responsive or Accessibility.

## Source

- [GitHub source](https://github.com/blame76/how-to-web/tree/main/blocks/product-card): Source files and research.

## Agent instruction

Reconstruct from Build DNA rather than copying HTML. Preserve purpose, constraints, behavior, stable geometry, responsive rules, accessibility and data honesty. Adapt framework and visual tokens to the target project. Ask for missing product requirements instead of inventing them.
